title: CMake: Prefer WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR and make it more convenient
description:
The CI runners used to derive the location for third party libraries
based on the WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR environment variable, but that hasn't
been the case for many years. Deprecate it in the Developer's Guide and
in CMake, and have WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR take precedence.

Allow WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR to be set using an environment variable or a
CMake variable on Windows and macOS.

notes.body: added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
Just noticed, we should get rid of the "Set *one* of these" line too.

With the support for WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR removed, how can I locally cache the libraries? Isn't WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR the path to the source code. I was very happy about the option to have local caches of the libs as this is a major speed-up in development.

For CI/CD jobs this might not make a difference but when working on multiple branches locally, the WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR was really useful.

Can I still achieve the same behavior without WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR?

With this change I also now get warnings from epan/CMakeLists.txt (maybe just something else wrong at my setup):

> CMake Error in epan/CMakeLists.txt: Target "epan" INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES property contains path:
>
> ```
> "***wireshark-source-path***/wireshark-x64-libs/vcpkg-export-2025.07.25-x64-windows-ws/installed/x64-windows/include/glib-2.0"
> ```
>
> which is prefixed in the source directory.

Support for WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR hasn't been removed (not yet, at least), but it is deprecated and if WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR is set the latter will take precedence.

Can you try setting WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR to the path you were using for WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR? The only difference is that an additional architecture and branch specific intermediate directory (e.g. wireshark-x64-libs on master and wireshark-x64-libs-4.6 on release-4.6) [will be created under WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt?ref_type=heads#L223).

As far as the "INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES property contains path ... which is prefixed in the source directory" error goes, that's [enforced by CMake](https://stackoverflow.com/a/25681179/82195) and applies to both variables. We should probably make it more clear in the documentation that neither WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR nor WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR can point to your source directory.

Thanks! Now I get it.

For many years my scripts were setting the WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR to the source directory. I am not sure, where that came from and I never questioned it. I will have to clean up some script now. :grinning:

I might have found a unintended (?) difference between `WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR` and `WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR`.

Example setup (Windows in this case and simplified):

* SOURCE_DIR: `E:\Wireshark-Devel\source\gitlab\test`
* BUILD_DIR: `E:\Wireshark-Devel\build\test`
* WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR: `..\..\..\wireshark-base-dir`
  * This is `E:\Wireshark-Devel\wireshark-base-dir`

When using this relative path, the executables of npcap and usbcap do not end up in the correct directory but in `BUILD_DIR\wireshark-base-dir\wireshark-x64-libs`.

However, all the extracted libraries end up at `E:\Wireshark-Devel\wireshark-base-dir\wireshark-x64-libs` as expected.

When I use an absolute path, it works.

When I replace `file(TO_CMAKE_PATH ${EXTRA_INSTALLER_DIR} _file_download_dir)` in CMakeLists.txt with `file(REAL_PATH ${EXTRA_INSTALLER_DIR} _file_download_dir)` it works too.

I used CMake 3.31.

Is this as intended or a bug?
